_meta.indication: REPATHA is indicated as an adjunct to diet and maximally tolerated statin therapy for adults with HeFH or clinical atherosclerotic CVD who require additional LDL-C lowering; and as an adjunct to diet and other LDL-lowering therapies for patients with HoFH who require additional LDL-C lowering.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, parallel group, placebo- and ezetimibe-controlled, multicenter, evaluating evolocumab monotherapy
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with a 10-year Framingham risk score of 10% or less (low cardiovascular risk)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary: percent change from baseline in reflexive LDL-C at Week 12, and mean percent change at Weeks 10 and 12
pivotal_trials.n: Study randomized 615 patients; 614 in full analysis set
pivotal_trials.result: Evolocumab 140 mg Q2W reduced LDL-C by -54% vs 0% placebo (p<0.0001); 420 mg QM -55% vs -1% placebo (p<0.0001); difference vs ezetimibe -36% (95% CL -52, -20)

nct_ctgov.title: Monoclonal Antibody Against PCSK9 to Reduce Elevated LDL-C in Subjects Currently Not Receiving Drug Therapy for Easing Lipid Levels-2

pivotal_trials.design: 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in HeFH patients on a stable statin dose
pivotal_trials.population: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) subjects on a stable dose of a statin
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary: percent change from baseline in reflexive LDL-C at Week 12, and mean percent change at Weeks 10 and 12
pivotal_trials.n: Study randomized 331 patients; 329 in full analysis set
pivotal_trials.result: Evolocumab 140 mg Q2W reduced LDL-C by -61% vs -2% placebo (p<0.0001), difference -59% (95% CL -75, -43); 420 mg QM -56% vs 4% placebo (p<0.0001), difference -60% (95% CL -76, -44)

nct_ctgov.title: Reduction of LDL-C With PCSK9 Inhibition in Heterozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia Disorder Study-2

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3 (Part B of a two-part phase 2/3 study)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label 8-patient pilot study (Part A) followed by a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (Part B); all subjects on a statin and about 93% also on ezetimibe
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH); baseline mean LDL-C 349 mg/dL despite statins
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change from baseline in (ultracentrifugation) LDL-C at Week 12
pivotal_trials.n: 50 patients randomized to evolocumab 420 mg QM (n=33) or placebo (n=17); full analysis set N=49
pivotal_trials.result: By FDA's analysis, LDL-C reduction was 30% greater on evolocumab (95% CI -42, -16); mean percent change -22% evolocumab vs 8% placebo

nct_ctgov.title: Trial Evaluating PCSK9 Antibody in Subjects With LDL Receptor Abnormalities

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>5%, more frequent than placebo): nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, influenza, back pain, and injection site reactions. In the 52-week trial: nasopharyngitis 10.5% vs 9.6% placebo, upper respiratory tract infection 9.3% vs 6.3%, influenza 7.5% vs 6.3%, back pain 6.2% vs 5.6%, injection site reactions 5.7% vs 5.0%. Allergic reactions (rash, urticaria) also occurred.
target_moa: Evolocumab is a human monoclonal IgG2 directed against PCSK9; it binds PCSK9 and inhibits circulating PCSK9 from binding the LDL receptor, preventing PCSK9-mediated LDLR degradation and increasing the number of LDLRs available to clear LDL, thereby lowering LDL-C.

advisory_committee.vote: Advisory Committee meeting held June 10, 2015. On whether benefit exceeded risk to support approval in one or more populations, the committee voted 11 'yes' and 4 'no'. For approval in HoFH, the committee voted 15 'yes' and 0 'no'.

summary.text: Standard-review BLA (not Priority) approved first cycle on 27 August 2015 based on the surrogate endpoint LDL-C across six phase 3 trials; evolocumab held orphan drug designation for HoFH, and approval was not under accelerated approval. The effect on cardiovascular morbidity and mortality had not been determined, and a large long-term outcomes trial was required as a PMR.
